description: This entry covers What Conservation Biology Studies as part of the fundamentals of conservation biology. In this field, biodiversity matters because the variety of genes, species, and ecosystems, the field's currency. overview: Conservation Biology is the field concerned with The science of saving biodiversity: protecting species, habitats, and ecosystems from extinction. What Conservation Biology Studies belongs to its essential core. Concretely: Biodiversity — the variety of genes, species, and ecosystems, the field's currency. And Population viability — modeling extinction risk from size, variation, and threats. Mastering this entry means being able to explain the topic in plain sentences, recognize it in real cases, and apply it alongside the neighboring ideas of the Foundations tier.
core_concepts: Biodiversity: the variety of genes, species, and ecosystems, the field's currency.
Population viability: modeling extinction risk from size, variation, and threats.
key_laws: Species-area relationship: species count rising with area to a power, predicting losses from habitat shrinkage.
vocabulary: Endemic: found nowhere else, hence irreplaceable.
Umbrella species: wide-ranging animals whose protection covers many others.
methods: Population surveys: estimating abundance and trends with mark-recapture and transects.
history: Conservation biology crystallized in the 1980s around Soulé, uniting ecology with crisis; island biogeography and population genetics supplied theory. It now spans rewilding, de-extinction debates, and 30x30 protection targets.

overview: Conservation Biology is the field concerned with The science of saving biodiversity: protecting species, habitats, and ecosystems from extinction. Current Research Frontiers in Conservation Biology belongs to its essential core. Concretely: Habitat loss and fragmentation — the leading driver, shrinking and isolating populations.
